o.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian قهوهای (qahva'ī). By surface analysis, qəhvə (“coffee”) + -i.
Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *yaŕtuk (“pillow”), cognate with Turkish yastık, etc.
Partial calque of Russian светофо́р (svetofór), substituting the first part with işıq (“light”). Compare Armenian լուսաֆոր (lusafor). Coined by Azerbaijani writer Rəsul Rza.
Borrowed from Russian гидрология (gidrologija). By surface analysis, hidro- + -logiya.
